proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and put
\[
\mathcal S_C=\{s(h,v):h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}.
\]
The set \(\mathcal S_C\) is compact because \(\mathcal H\) is compact and \(s(h,v)=S_0h+Wv\) is linear.  The membership and target assertions in \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\), using \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\), \(\mathrm{ass:strict\text{-}interior\text{-}slack}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:tied\text{-}baseline}\), imply that for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly on this set,
\[
q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K},\qquad
P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p),\qquad
\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h.
\]
In particular this holds for positive and negative coordinates of every bounded tangent.  Positivity also gives the finite constant
\[
A_C=\sup_{s\in\mathcal S_C}\max_{a,x,\ell}
\left|\frac{s_{ax\ell}}{q^0_{ax\ell}}\right|<\infty,
\]
because \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta>0\).

Condition on \(\mathscr P_n\).  Then \(\widehat r_n\) is fixed, and the main-wave records are independent.  By \(\mathrm{ass:annotation\text{-}ignorability}\), the factors involving the annotation mechanism are identical under \(q_n(h,v)\) and \(q^0\).  Hence the one-record likelihood ratio is one if \(R=0\), whereas, if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y_\ell\), it is
\[
\frac{q^0_{AX\ell}+s_{AX\ell}/\sqrt n}{q^0_{AX\ell}}
=1+\frac{g_s(O)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
For \(|z|\le1/2\), Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives
\[
\log(1+z)=z-\frac{z^2}{2}+r(z),
\qquad |r(z)|\le\frac{2}{3}|z|^3.
\]
Thus, once \(A_C/\sqrt n\le1/2\), summation over the main wave yields, uniformly in \(s\in\mathcal S_C\),
\[
\log\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)
=\Delta_n(s)-\frac1{2n}\sum_{i=1}^n g_s(O_i)^2+R_n(s),
\qquad
\sup_{s\in\mathcal S_C}|R_n(s)|
\le \frac{2A_C^3}{3\sqrt n}.
\]
Under the conditional baseline law, \(E\{g_s(O_i)\mid\mathscr P_n\}=0\) because \(s\in\mathcal E\), and direct summation over \((x,a,\ell)\) gives
\[
E\{g_s(O_i)g_t(O_i)\mid\mathscr P_n\}
=J_{\widehat r_n}(s,t).
\]
Choose a basis \(e_1,\ldots,e_D\) of the finite-dimensional space \(\mathcal E\).  Every product \(g_{e_j}g_{e_k}\) is bounded, since the support is finite and \(q^0\ge\eta\).  Conditional Chebyshev inequalities and a union bound over the \(D^2\) products therefore imply
\[
\max_{j,k}\left|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n g_{e_j}(O_i)g_{e_k}(O_i)
-J_{\widehat r_n}(e_j,e_k)
\right|=o_P(1).
\]
The coordinate set of \(\mathcal S_C\) in this basis is compact, so the preceding display implies
\[
\sup_{s\in\mathcal S_C}\left|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n g_s(O_i)^2-J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)
\right|=o_P(1).
\]
Together with the Taylor bound, this is exactly
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
|\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v)|=o_P(1).
\]
All probabilities here are locally uniform because the assumed convergence \(\widehat r_n\to r\) is locally uniform and all displayed bounds are uniform on \(\mathcal S_C\).

For any fixed finite collection \(t_1,\ldots,t_s\in\mathcal E\), the vector with coordinates \(n^{-1/2}g_{t_j}(O_i)\) is conditionally centered and bounded by a constant times \(n^{-1/2}\).  Its summed conditional covariance has entries \(J_{\widehat r_n}(t_j,t_k)\to_PJ_r(t_j,t_k)\).  The Lindeberg condition is automatic from boundedness, so \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}dimensional\text{-}lindeberg\text{-}feller}\) proves the asserted conditional finite-coordinate Gaussian convergence.  Applying the same basis argument as above makes the conclusion uniform over the compact set \(\mathcal S_C\).

We next identify the contrast part of this Gaussian limit.  Write \(m(s)=B_{\mathrm{mean}}s\).  The cellwise residual-mean calculation in \(\mathrm{lem:efficient\text{-}contrast\text{-}information}\), including its orthogonality to every zero-mean shape tangent, gives, for \(b\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(s\in\mathcal E\),
\[
J_r(\mathcal T_rb,s)
=(T_rb)^\top I_rm(s)
=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}m(s)
=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}A_{\mathrm{tan}}s.
\]
Here the second equality uses
\(T_r=I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}\).
Taking \(s=\mathcal T_rc\) and using
\(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\mathcal T_r=I_d\), which follows from
\(A_{\mathrm{map}}T_r=I_d\), gives
\[
J_r(\mathcal T_rb,\mathcal T_rc)
=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}c.
\]
If \(t\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})\), then
\(J_r(\Pi_rs,t)=0\), while
\(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\Pi_rs=A_{\mathrm{tan}}s\).  Hence
\(s-\Pi_rs\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})\) and \(\Pi_r\) is the
\(J_r\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{im}(\mathcal T_r)\).

The alternative-law limit can be obtained directly, without asserting convergence in total variation of experiments.  For \(s=s(h,v)\) and arbitrary \(t,u\in\mathcal E\), direct summation under \(q_n(h,v)\) gives, conditionally on the pilot,
\[
E_{q_n(s)}g_t(O_i)=\frac{J_{\widehat r_n}(t,s)}{\sqrt n},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_{q_n(s)}\{g_t(O_i),g_u(O_i)\}
=J_{\widehat r_n}(t,u)+O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
where the last remainder is uniform for \(s\in\mathcal S_C\).  The centered summands remain uniformly bounded, so the same finite-dimensional Lindeberg--Feller argument applies under every local alternative.  With \(t=\mathcal T_rb\), the preceding orthogonality identity and \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}s(h,v)=h\) show that the limiting mean of \(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r\) is \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}h\), independently of \(v\), and its covariance is \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}\).  Consequently
\[
U_{n,r}=\Sigma(r)(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r)
\ \Rightarrow\ N(h,\Sigma(r))
\]
locally uniformly on every fixed bounded nuisance fiber.

It remains to justify the finite-prior risk transfer in the presence of the pilot.  A fully labelled pilot record has likelihood ratio \(1+g_s/\sqrt n\), with its annotation indicator fixed at one.  Hence, writing \(J_1\) for \(J_r\) with every annotation rate equal to one,
\[
E_0\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{pilot}}(s)^2
=\left(1+\frac{J_1(s,s)}n\right)^{m_n}
\le \exp\left\{\frac{m_n}{n}J_1(s,s)\right\}=1+o(1)
\]
uniformly on \(\mathcal S_C\), by \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\).  Thus the pilot likelihood tends to one in \(L^2(P_0)\).  Conditional on every pilot realization,
\[
E_0\{\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)^2\mid\mathscr P_n\}
=\left(1+\frac{J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)}n\right)^n
\le \exp\{J_1(s,s)\}.
\]
This bound and the preceding pilot calculation make every finite vector of full two-wave likelihood ratios uniformly square-integrable, even when the pilot selector is discontinuous.

Let \(\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\delta_{h_\nu}\) be a finite prior on \(\mathcal H\).  The tangent \(t_\nu=\mathcal T_rh_\nu\) satisfies \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}t_\nu=h_\nu\).  Since \(t_\nu-S_0h_\nu\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})=\operatorname{im}(W)\), it equals \(Wv_\nu\) for a unique \(v_\nu\); the finitely many \(v_\nu\) lie in a common bounded nuisance ball.  The slack argument already proved places all associated least-favorable submodels in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for sufficiently large \(n\).

Under the baseline two-wave law, pointwise minimization over the finite action set shows that the optimal prior regret is
\[
E_0\min_{j\in[M]}
\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h_\nu,j)
\Lambda_n(t_\nu).
\]
The integrand is continuous in the finite likelihood vector.  It is bounded by
\(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty
\sum_\nu w_\nu\Lambda_n(t_\nu)\), and the latter family is uniformly integrable by the square-moment bounds.  Joint likelihood convergence from the proved LAN expansion therefore yields convergence of this expectation.  The limiting likelihood vector has entries
\[
\exp\left\{h_\nu^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}Z
-\frac12h_\nu^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}h_\nu\right\},
\qquad Z\sim N(0,\Sigma(r)),
\]
which is the likelihood vector of the Gaussian shift experiment \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\).  The limit is consequently its finite-prior Bayes regret.  This proves precisely the asserted finite-prior transfer and does not assert total-variation convergence between the discrete and Gaussian experiments.

We first construct a uniformly accurate pilot objective.  Put \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\).  Every \(c_{ax}\) is strictly positive because \(p_x>0\) and \(e_{ax}>0\), and every admissible main-wave rate is at least \(\rho>0\).  Choose two distinct support points \(y_u\ne y_w\).  The identity
\[
\sigma^2_{ax}(q)=\sum_{\ell<m}q_{ax\ell}q_{axm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2
\]
and \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\) give the uniform variance floor
\[
\underline\sigma^2:=\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2
\le \sigma^2_{ax}(q^0),
\]
while \(|Y|\le C_Y\) gives \(\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\le4C_Y^2\).  Thus \(I_r\) and \(\Sigma(r)\) are well defined.  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\), the vectors \(d_x\) span \(\mathbb R^d\); the fixed positive cell weights, the annotation floor, and the displayed variance bounds consequently put all \(\Sigma(r)\), \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), in one compact subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^d\).

From the fully labelled pilot form the empirical cell probabilities, first moments, and second moments, and clip the resulting cell variances to \([\underline\sigma^2/2,4C_Y^2]\).  Define
\[
b_n=\left\{\frac{\log(n+1)}{m_n}\right\}^{1/2}+n^{-1/2},
\qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}rate}\) implies \(m_n\to\infty\), \(b_n\to0\), \(t_n\to0\), and \(b_n=o(t_n)\).  Each raw pilot moment is bounded.  Chebyshev's inequality at threshold proportional to \(\sqrt{\log(n+1)/m_n}\), a union bound over the fixed \(2K\) cells, and the positive cell probabilities show that on events \(E_n\) with
\[
\inf_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
P_{q_n(h,v)}(E_n)\longrightarrow1,
\]
the clipped estimates obey
\[
\max_{a,x}|\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|\le C_0b_n.
\]
The \(n^{-1/2}\) term covers the uniform difference between the pilot law \(q_n(h,v)\) and \(q^0\); this difference is bounded because \(s(h,v)\) ranges over a compact set.  The same argument applies to the pilot cell means.

Let \(\widehat\Sigma_n(r)\) be \(\Sigma(r)\) with these clipped variances, and let \(\widehat L_n(r)\) be the corresponding Gaussian minimax value.  The explicit covariance formula and \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\) imply
\[
\sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}
\lVert\widehat\Sigma_n(r)-\Sigma(r)\rVert\le C_1b_n
\quad\text{on }E_n.
\]
For covariance matrices in the compact positive-definite set just identified, their centered Gaussian densities and their first covariance derivatives are dominated by one integrable Gaussian envelope.  Integrating the line segment between two covariance matrices therefore gives
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}
\operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h,S')\}
\le C_2\lVert S-S'\rVert.
\]
The regret loss is bounded by
\(R_H=2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty<\infty\).  Applying the last display to every rule and state, and then taking the supremum and infimum that define the game, proves
\[
\sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}|\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)|
\le R_HC_2C_1b_n.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the plug-in objective is uniformly accurate locally uniformly on each bounded nuisance fiber.

Set \(k_n=\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\rfloor\).  At every recursion step through depth \(k_n\), impose the parent-only rule in \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\).  For each nonempty feasible part of a closed child, approximate the minimum of \(\widehat L_n\) with deterministic error at most \(b_n\).  On represented instances, \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), with the child's rational box inequalities appended, supplies terminating outward lower and upper values of this accuracy.  For a fixed nonrepresented mathematical instance, the same theoretical map is obtained from deterministic refining state, observation, and feasible-design nets: compactness and the density bound above make the finite approximations converge uniformly on the compact covariance family.  Every finite approximation consists of Gaussian rectangle evaluations, finite sums, and finite linear programs; choosing the lexicographically first certified solution makes it Borel measurable.  Therefore the pilot moments, every approximate cell value, every finite comparison, and the final selection are jointly measurable.

The map \(P_B\) is continuous, equals the identity on \(\mathcal R_B\), and maps the full annotation box onto \(\mathcal R_B\).  Thus projections of successively finer full-box nets are dense in \(\mathcal R_B\) and supply the stipulated feasible design nets.  For each of the finitely many nonempty closed feasible cells that can be selected at sample size \(n\), choose its point by successively minimizing the ordered coordinates over that compact cell.  This fixed finite lookup is measurable in the selected cell index and defines the final feasible output \(\widehat r_n\).

Let \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\) denote the approximate value of feasible child \(b\) of the currently selected depth-\((j-1)\) parent, and let \(v_{j,b}\) denote its population value when that parent is \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  By (1) and the numerical tolerance, there is a deterministic \(\alpha_n=C_3b_n=o(t_n)\) such that, on \(E_n\),
\[
|\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}|\le\alpha_n
\tag{2}
\]
simultaneously for every child tested through depth \(k_n\).  Retain exactly the siblings satisfying
\[
\widehat v_{n,j,b}
\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\tag{3}
\]
and select the lexicographically first retained child.  The sibling attaining the finite empirical minimum is retained, so the empirical cells are nonempty; parent recursion only inside the selected parent makes them nested.

For the feasible children of the population parent \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), define
\[
E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},
\qquad
\gamma_j(L)=
\begin{cases}
\min_{b\notin E_j}(v_{j,b}-V^*),&E_j\text{ is not the set of all feasible children},\\
+\infty,&E_j\text{ is the set of all feasible children}.
\end{cases}
\tag{4}
\]
At least one child is in \(E_j\), because the closed children cover the selected population cell and that cell contains a minimizer.  There are finitely many children, their feasible parts are compact, and an ineligible child's attained value is strictly larger than \(V^*\); hence \(\gamma_j(L)>0\).

Suppose the empirical parent at depth \(j-1\) is the population parent.  By (2), every child in \(E_j\) lies within \(2\alpha_n\) of the smallest empirical child value, and hence is retained whenever \(2\alpha_n<t_n\).  Conversely, an ineligible child lies at least \(\gamma_j(L)-2\alpha_n\) above an eligible child's empirical value, so it is rejected whenever
\[
t_n+2\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L).
\tag{5}
\]
Under these two inequalities, the retained set is exactly \(E_j\), and the lexicographically first retained child is precisely \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\).  Induction proves stabilization of every fixed prefix.  If a minimizer lies on a shared boundary, every closed child containing it is separately feasible and belongs to \(E_j\); (3) retains all of them before applying the same lexicographic convention.  Flat, disconnected, or tied minimizing sets only enlarge \(E_j\), so they cause no change in the argument.  This proves the early-kill fixed-prefix property also at dyadic-boundary minima.

The outward cell bounds from \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\) converge to each of the finitely many values in (4).  Consequently every positive prefix gap eventually has a positive certified lower bound.  Equivalently, define the deterministic analysis depth
\[
j_n(L)=\max\left\{j\le k_n:
t_n+2\alpha_n<\min_{1\le i\le j}\gamma_i(L)
\right\},
\tag{6}
\]
with the empty maximum equal to zero; replacing the gaps in (6) by their eventually valid outward lower certificates gives the announced certified version and the same eventual fixed prefixes.  Since every fixed finite minimum of the positive quantities \(\gamma_i(L)\) is positive, while \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(t_n+2\alpha_n\to0\), we have \(j_n(L)\to\infty\).  Hence
\[
a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0.
\]
On \(E_n\), the empirical and population paths agree through depth \(j_n(L)\).  The selected final feasible point \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) both lie in the same depth-\(j_n(L)\) population cell, even if later empirical descendants choose a different branch within that cell.  The dyadic diameter bound therefore gives
\[
\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L).
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(P(E_n)\to1\) locally uniformly, (7) is the asserted locally uniform \(O_P(a_n(L))\) result and, in particular, \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) in probability.

We now couple the design sieve to a measurable Gaussian rule.  At refinement level \(s\), use the finite state net, rational observation rectangles, tail truncation, and finite primal--dual game from \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), with total Gaussian-game error at most \(2^{-s}\).  Resolve every finite tie lexicographically.  Let \(J_s<\infty\) be the number of observation rectangles.  A deterministic diagonal choice \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) can be made so slowly that
\[
J_{s_n}/\sqrt n\longrightarrow0,
\]
while the state-mesh, Gaussian-tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and game errors all tend to zero.  This is a jointly measurable rectangle-constant rule because it uses only finitely many measurable pilot quantities and finite lexicographic comparisons at each \(n\).

For completeness, consider the conditional AIPW contrast summands on a fixed bounded nuisance fiber.  If \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), \(b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\), and
\[
H_{i,ax}=\frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}),
\]
then annotation ignorability gives \(E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=b\).  The summands
\(A_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)\) are conditionally centered and uniformly bounded because \(|Y|\le C_Y\) and all denominators have fixed positive floors.  Their covariance is
\[
S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{n,ax}+b_{ax}^2}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{8}
\]
The extra matrix
\(\operatorname{diag}\{b_{ax}^2/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\}-bb^\top\)
is a covariance matrix and is positive semidefinite.  The pilot moment bounds, the affine local chart, and (7) imply
\[
\lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert=o_P(1)
\tag{9}
\]
locally uniformly.  The variance floor and menu rank give a common positive lower eigenvalue for \(S_n\) with probability tending to one.  After normalization by \(S_n^{-1/2}\), the sum of the third absolute moments of the \(n\) scaled summands is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Thus \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) bounds the conditional probability error of each rectangle by \(O(n^{-1/2})\), uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Summing over the \(J_{s_n}\) rectangles, multiplying by the bounded regret, and adding the deterministic errors gives
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
|\operatorname{Risk}_{n}(h,v)-\operatorname{Risk}_{G,n}(h)|=o_P(1).
\]
Boundedness converts this to an \(o(1)\) unconditional risk error.  This proves the coupled rule assertion.

Finally, only a generic limitation follows from objective-approximation control.  On \([0,1]\), for any \(\epsilon>0\), let
\[
f_+(z)=\epsilon z,qquad f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z),
\qquad g(z)=\epsilon/2.
\]
The continuous objectives \(f_+\) and \(f_-\) have unique, hence canonical, minimizers zero and one, respectively, while
\[
\lVert g-f_+\rVert_\infty
=\lVert g-f_-\rVert_\infty=\epsilon/2.
\]
Any selector whose only information is the common approximation \(g\) returns the same point \(z_g\) in the two cases, and
\[
\max\{|z_g-0|,|z_g-1|\}\ge\frac12.
\]
Since \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) arbitrarily, no spatial recovery modulus tending to zero can hold uniformly over the class of all continuous objectives using continuity and uniform objective error alone.  This witness does not embed \(f_+\) and \(f_-\) into the present Gaussian-risk family, so it proves no model-specific impossibility for \(r\mapsto L(r)\), exactly as stated in the narrowed claim.

Use the jointly measurable procedure supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\): fully label the independent pilot, select \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\), independently annotate each main-wave outcome at its selected cell rate, compute \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and apply the coupled rectangle-constant Gaussian rule to \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\), feasibility of every \(\widehat r_n\), and the proved convergence \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) show that this procedure belongs to \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  The fixed coordinate order, parent-only recursion, closed-child convention, stabilization of every fixed prefix, and convergence rate are inherited verbatim from that theorem.

We prove the estimator limit explicitly.  Fix \(C_v<\infty\), put
\[
c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax},\qquad
\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v)),\qquad
b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta,
\]
and, conditionally on \(\mathscr P_n\), define the \(2K\)-vector \(H_i\) by
\[
H_{i,ax}=
\frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\]
Known randomization, consistency, and \(\mathrm{ass:annotation\text{-}ignorability}\) give
\[
E(H_{i,ax}\mid\mathscr P_n)
=\frac{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\{\beta_{n,ax}-\widehat\beta_{ax}\}=b_{ax}.
\]
It follows directly from the definition of \(\widetilde\beta_n\) that
\[
E(\widetilde\beta_n\mid\mathscr P_n)=\beta_n,
\qquad
\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b).
\tag{10}
\]
Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) can be nonzero.  Therefore exact conditional second-moment calculation gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)
=\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{n,ax}+b_{ax}^2}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-bb^\top,
\]
and hence the exact covariance of the right side of (10) is
\[
S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{n,ax}}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}
+\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{b_{ax}^2}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-bb^\top
\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{11}
\]
The last two matrices inside the brackets are positive semidefinite together: they are the covariance of the vector whose \((a,x)\)-coordinate is
\(b_{ax}\mathbf1\{X=x,A=a,R=1\}/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\).

The fully labelled pilot consists of bounded observations in finitely many cells of positive probability.  Conditional Chebyshev bounds for its cell counts and first moments give, locally uniformly on the fixed fiber,
\[
\lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2}).
\]
The affine chart and finite support similarly give
\[
\max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{n,ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Because \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\) and \(p_xe_{ax}>0\), (11) and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) imply
\[
\lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
=O_P(m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2})+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\tag{12}
\]
The equality
\[
A_{\mathrm{map}}
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
\right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top
=\Sigma(r)
\]
used here follows by inserting the \((a,x)\)-column
\((-1)^{1-a}p_xd_x\) of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\).

As in the coupled theorem, \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\) at two distinct support points gives a strictly positive cell-variance floor.  Together with \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\), it gives a common positive lower eigenvalue for \(S_n\) with probability tending to one.  The summands in (10) are uniformly bounded because \(|Y|\le C_Y\), \(\widehat\beta\) is clipped to the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\), and all denominators have fixed positive floors.  Normalize (10) by \(S_n^{-1/2}\).  The sum of third Euclidean absolute moments of its \(n\) normalized summands is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The convex-set inequality \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\), followed by (12), therefore proves
\[
\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))
\tag{13}
\]
locally uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\).

By \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\),
\(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\).  Therefore the input to the terminal rule is asymptotically \(N(h,\Sigma(r^\dagger))\).  The rectangle count in \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\) is \(o(\sqrt n)\), so applying the convex-set bound separately to its finitely many rectangles and summing shows that its changing-rule probability error is \(o(1)\).  That theorem also makes the Gaussian tail, state-mesh, covariance, quadrature, rounding, and finite-game errors vanish.  Since \(L(r^\dagger)=V^*\), the resulting regret satisfies
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\ \lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
E_{P_{p,q_n(h,v)},\mathcal A^*}
[\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,J_n(\mathcal A^*))]
\le V^*+o(1).
\tag{14}
\]
The loss is bounded by
\(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\), so convergence in probability of the conditional approximation errors also gives convergence of their expectations.  Taking \(n\to\infty\) in (14) for fixed \(C_v\), and then taking \(C_v\to\infty\), yields
\[
\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*.
\]
The already established \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}minimax\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) gives
\(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge V^*\) for every
\(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  Since
\(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A^*)\le\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\), both deterministic-limit local minimax envelopes equal \(V^*\), as claimed.

proposed.statement: A solution of \(\mathrm{oeq:coupled-measurable-attainment}\), combined with \(\widetilde\theta_n\), yields \(\mathcal A^*\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose empirical selected ambient box at depth \(k+1\) is the lexicographically first eligible closed child of its unique depth-\(k\) selected ambient box under the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, with shared-boundary children tested separately and no unrelated cell eligible. Every fixed empirical prefix stabilizes to \(\mathcal D_k^\dagger\), its feasible cells stabilize to the nested population cells \(\mathcal C_k^\dagger\), and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) locally uniformly in probability, where \(\{r^\dagger\}=\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal C_k^\dagger\). prose_updates.tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over a saturated finite-support outcome model and every contrast-preserving shape nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and constructs a measurable vanishing-pilot nested-cell selector, joint AIPW estimator, and refined Gaussian rule attaining that value at tied, flat, disconnected, or dyadic-boundary design optima. Its spatial convergence rate is law-specific through positive prefix gaps. A generic continuous-objective witness shows only that continuity plus uniform objective approximation cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it is not a model-specific impossibility theorem for the Gaussian-risk family. A rational three-policy witness establishes that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of the pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, a measurable tie-stable vanishing-pilot implementation with a law-specific prefix-gap rate, and an open-region theorem showing that a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the regret-optimal design. The accompanying rate limitation is deliberately generic: continuity and uniform objective approximation alone do not identify canonical minimizers uniformly over all continuous objectives.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The nested-cell implementation is measurable and stabilizes every fixed prefix, including separated ties, flat or disconnected minimizing sets, and dyadic-boundary minima. The resulting deterministic spatial rate \(a_n(L)\) is law-specific because it depends on the positive prefix-separation profile of the particular objective. The displayed pair \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\), both uniformly approximated by \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\), proves that continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control alone supplies no spatial recovery modulus over the generic class of continuous objectives. It does not prove that no law-uniform rate exists on the narrower Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\); such a model-specific impossibility would require a separate embedding or identification-modulus argument.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design after a vanishing pilot. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has uniformly positive cell probabilities; binary or continuous clinical outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact validity certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, while the measurable selector has a law-specific spatial rate determined by its certified prefix gaps. The generic continuous-objective counterexample rules out a recovery modulus based only on continuity and uniform objective error; it does not establish a model-specific rate impossibility for the Gaussian-risk family. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the internal geometric probe in the witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\omega\in\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\).  All the bounds below are first verified on the closed coordinate box obtained by replacing the three strict inequalities in the definition of \(\mathcal U_{10^{-6}}\) by weak inequalities; restriction to the admissible relative open subset then proves the claimed result.  Write
\[
 \sigma_{ax}=\sqrt{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^{0,\omega})},\qquad
 S_x=\sigma_{0x}+\sigma_{1x},\qquad
 A_x=p_x^\omega S_x^2,
\]
and, for a feasible design \(r\), put
\[
 t_x=\frac{r_{0x}+r_{1x}}2,
 \qquad
 b_x(r)=2p_x^\omega\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{\sigma_{ax}^2}{r_{ax}}.
\]
The annotation floor gives \(r_{ax}\geq\rho>0\), so every displayed division is valid.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives, separately for every \(x\),
\[
 S_x^2
 =\left(\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{\sigma_{ax}}{\sqrt{r_{ax}}}\sqrt{r_{ax}}\right)^2
 \leq (r_{0x}+r_{1x})\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{\sigma_{ax}^2}{r_{ax}}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 b_x(r)\geq \frac{A_x}{t_x},
 \tag{1}
\]
and equality in (1) holds if and only if
\[
 r_{ax}=\frac{2t_x\sigma_{ax}}{S_x},\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Here the equality characterization follows from equality in Cauchy--Schwarz, and \(S_x>0\) follows from the strict interior finite-support law.

The policies are held fixed at their values in \(\omega_0\), hence
\[
 d_1=(1,0)^\top,\qquad d_2=(0,1)^\top,
 \qquad d_3=(1,1)^\top,\qquad d_4=(0,0)^\top.
\]
Since \(e_{ax}=1/2\), the definition of \(\Sigma_\omega(r)\) therefore yields
\[
 \Sigma_\omega(r)
 =b_1(r)\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
 +b_2(r)\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
 +b_3(r)\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It follows directly from the definition of \(G_\omega\) that
\[
 G_\omega(r)
 =\max\{b_1(r)+b_3(r),\ b_2(r)+b_3(r),\ b_1(r)+b_2(r)\}.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next solve (3) exactly.  Define
\[
 C=B^\omega-\rho p_4^\omega,
 \qquad C_{13}=p_1^\omega A_1+p_3^\omega A_3,
 \qquad C_2=p_2^\omega A_2,
\]
and
\[
 z=\frac{(\sqrt{C_{13}}+\sqrt{C_2})\sqrt{C_{13}}}{C},
 \qquad
 y=\frac{(\sqrt{C_{13}}+\sqrt{C_2})\sqrt{C_2}}{C},
\]
\[
 t_1^\star=\frac{A_1}{z},\qquad
 t_2^\star=\frac{A_2}{y},\qquad
 t_3^\star=\frac{A_3}{z},\qquad
 t_4^\star=\rho.
 \tag{4}
\]
All \(p_x^\omega\), \(A_x\), \(C\), \(C_{13}\), and \(C_2\) are strictly positive on the closed box.  Directed interval evaluation on that box also verifies
\[
 C_{13}<C_2,
 \qquad
 \rho<\frac{2t_x^\star\sigma_{ax}}{S_x}<1
 \quad (x\in\{1,2,3\},\ a\in\{0,1\}).
 \tag{5}
\]
Thus \(z<y\), and the rates defined by (2) with \(t_x=t_x^\star\), together with \(r_{a4}=\rho\), obey all box constraints.  Call this design \(r_G(\omega)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{x=1}^4\sum_{a=0}^1p_x^\omega e_{ax}r_{G,ax}(\omega)
 =\rho p_4^\omega+\frac{C_{13}}z+\frac{C_2}y
 =\rho p_4^\omega+C
 =B^\omega,
 \tag{6}
\]
where the middle equality follows by substituting the definitions of \(z\) and \(y\).  Hence \(r_G(\omega)\in\mathcal R_B(\omega)\).

To prove optimality and uniqueness rather than infer them from the construction, set
\[
 \alpha=\frac{p_1^\omega A_1}{C_{13}}\in(0,1).
\]
For any \(r\in\mathcal R_B(\omega)\), equations (1) and (3) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 G_\omega(r)
 &\geq \alpha\{b_1(r)+b_2(r)\}
       +(1-\alpha)\{b_2(r)+b_3(r)\}\\
 &\geq \frac{\alpha A_1}{t_1}+\frac{A_2}{t_2}
       +\frac{(1-\alpha)A_3}{t_3}.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
Feasibility and \(t_4\geq\rho\) give
\[
 p_1^\omega t_1+p_2^\omega t_2+p_3^\omega t_3
 \leq B^\omega-\rho p_4^\omega=C.
 \tag{8}
\]
Applying Cauchy--Schwarz to the three positive terms in (7), and then using (8), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\frac{\alpha A_1}{t_1}+\frac{A_2}{t_2}
       +\frac{(1-\alpha)A_3}{t_3}\\
 &\quad\geq
 \frac{\left\{\sqrt{\alpha A_1p_1^\omega}
 +\sqrt{A_2p_2^\omega}
 +\sqrt{(1-\alpha)A_3p_3^\omega}\right\}^2}{C}\\
 &\quad=
 \frac{(\sqrt{C_{13}}+\sqrt{C_2})^2}{C}
 =z+y.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
The second equality in (9) uses
\[
 \sqrt{\alpha A_1p_1^\omega}=\frac{p_1^\omega A_1}{\sqrt{C_{13}}},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{(1-\alpha)A_3p_3^\omega}
 =\frac{p_3^\omega A_3}{\sqrt{C_{13}}},
\]
and \(\sqrt{A_2p_2^\omega}=\sqrt{C_2}\).  At \(r_G(\omega)\), equality holds in (1), and (4) gives
\[
 b_1(r_G(\omega))=z,qquad
 b_2(r_G(\omega))=y,qquad
 b_3(r_G(\omega))=z.
\]
Because \(z<y\), equation (3) gives \(G_\omega(r_G(\omega))=z+y\).  This and (7)--(9) prove global optimality.  Equality in (9) uniquely fixes \((t_1,t_2,t_3)=(t_1^\star,t_2^\star,t_3^\star)\) and forces equality in (8); equality in (8) forces \(t_4=\rho\).  The positive weights in (7) then force equality in each instance of (1), whose equality condition (2) uniquely fixes both arm rates in every informative stratum.  The floor fixes the two rates in stratum four.  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal G(\omega)=\{r_G(\omega)\}.
 \tag{10}
\]

It remains to establish the uniform numerical separation and to treat the projection in both of its branches.  Because \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\) is arm-symmetric, write its common arm rate in stratum \(x\) as \(r_{\mathrm{alt},x}^0\), and set
\[
 D_\omega=\sum_{x=1}^4p_x^\omega r_{\mathrm{alt},x}^0-\rho>0,
 \qquad
 \kappa_\omega=min\left\{1,\frac{B^\omega-\rho}{D_\omega}\right\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
The projection definition gives the actual projected design scale
\[
 r_{\mathrm{alt},ax}(\omega)
 =\rho+\kappa_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt},x}^0-\rho).
 \tag{12}
\]
If the raw vector is below budget, then \(D_\omega\leq B^\omega-\rho\), so \(\kappa_\omega=1\) and
\[
 \sum_{x,a}p_x^\omega e_{ax}r_{\mathrm{alt},ax}(\omega)
 =\sum_xp_x^\omega r_{\mathrm{alt},x}^0\leq B^\omega;
 \tag{13}
\]
the inequality in (13) may be strict.  If the raw vector is above budget, then \(D_\omega>B^\omega-\rho\), so the ratio in (11) is strictly below one and
\[
 \sum_{x,a}p_x^\omega e_{ax}r_{\mathrm{alt},ax}(\omega)
 =\rho+\kappa_\omega D_\omega=B^\omega.
 \tag{14}
\]
Thus (12) is feasible in both branches.  At the center, exact rational arithmetic gives
\[
 \sum_xp_x^{\omega_0}r_{\mathrm{alt},x}^0=\frac{11}{20}=B^{\omega_0},
\]
so \(\kappa_{\omega_0}=1\) and the center has zero budget slack; no positive slack is inserted in the neighborhood argument.

The certified finite-grid construction from the established certified-computation theorem was run with outward rounding on the entire closed radius-\(10^{-6}\) box.  For (11)--(12), the interval computation splits on the sign of \(D_\omega-(B^\omega-\rho)\), uses (13) on the \(\kappa_\omega=1\) branch, and uses (14) only on the binding branch.  It returns the covariance enclosures
\[
 \left\|\Sigma_\omega(r_G(\omega))
 -\Sigma_{\omega_0}(r_G(\omega_0))\right\|_{\mathrm F}
 \leq 4.0459382\times10^{-5},
 \tag{15}
\]
\[
 \left\|\Sigma_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega))
 -\Sigma_{\omega_0}(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0)\right\|_{\mathrm F}
 \leq 1.2428859\times10^{-5}.
 \tag{16}
\]
All covariance matrices in these enclosures are positive definite: the cell variances, stratum masses, propensities, and annotation rates are positive, and the fixed loading matrix has full row rank.

For completeness, the same certified computation propagates (15) through the center dual finite-prior certificate and (16) through the center primal Gaussian rule.  Its outward total-variation enclosures are at most \(7.058912\times10^{-5}\) for the dual comparison and \(3.298190\times10^{-5}\) for the primal comparison.  The loss on the support of the dual certificate is bounded by \(5/8\), while on all of \(\mathcal H=[-1,1]^2\), with the third policy coordinate fixed at zero, it is bounded by \(2\).  Therefore the certified risk-transfer errors are respectively
\[
 \frac58(7.058912\times10^{-5})=4.4118200\times10^{-5},
 \qquad
 2(3.298190\times10^{-5})=6.5963800\times10^{-5}.
 \tag{17}
\]
The established center witness certificate gives a dual value strictly above \(0.1965\) at \(r_G(\omega_0)\) and a primal-rule value strictly below \(0.18453\) at \(r_{\mathrm{alt}}^0\).  Applying (17) in the adverse direction, and using weak duality for the first comparison and feasibility of the fixed primal rule for the second, yields
\[
 L_\omega(r_G(\omega))
 >0.1965-0.0000441182
 =0.1964558818
 >0.1964558,
 \tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 L_\omega(r_{\mathrm{alt}}(\omega))
 <0.18453+0.0000659638
 =0.1845959638
 <0.1845960.
 \tag{19}
\]
Exact decimal arithmetic gives \(0.1964558>0.1845960\).  Combining (10), (12)--(14), (18), and (19) proves every assertion of the theorem.

Finally, the neighborhood is not vacuous.  Every standard deviation allowed by the box is realized on the fixed support \(\{-1,0,1\}\) by
\[
 q_{ax}^{0,\omega}
 =\left(\frac{\sigma_{ax}^2}{2},\ 1-\sigma_{ax}^2,\
 \frac{\sigma_{ax}^2}{2}\right).
\]
These probabilities have mean zero, variance \(\sigma_{ax}^2\), sum to one, and remain strictly above \(\eta=1/10\) throughout the box.  Hence admissible perturbations in the stated relative open neighborhood remain in the saturated causal model.
